faqs.a: Use an absolute https:// URL — relative paths are the number one reason cards show no image. Keep it under 5 MB, ideally 1200x630 px for large cards. And the URL must be publicly reachable: crawlers can't log in.
faqs.q: Why is my card image not showing?

faqs.a: Open Graph (og:) tags are the open standard that Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, and most platforms read. Twitter Cards (twitter:) tags refine the display on X. Set both: og: tags as the base, twitter:card and twitter: overrides for X.
faqs.q: What is the difference between Open Graph and Twitter Cards?

faqs.a: X caches cards aggressively (about 7 days). Use X's Card Validator to refresh the cache for a URL. Facebook's Sharing Debugger similarly rescrapes and shows you what Facebook sees.
faqs.q: I fixed my tags but the old card still shows — why?

faqs.a: summary shows a small square thumbnail beside the text — good for articles. summary_large_image shows a wide banner image above the text — better for visual content and usually higher click-through. This tool previews both.
faqs.q: summary vs summary_large_image — which should I use?

faqs.a: WhatsApp and Telegram read og: tags. WhatsApp shows the og:image with title and domain; keep images under 300 KB for fast rendering. Telegram additionally supports larger images. iMessage uses its own heuristics but also reads og: tags.
faqs.q: What about WhatsApp, Telegram, and iMessage previews?

faqs.a: Yes, with limits: it parses the tags and renders faithful mock cards, but it can't replicate each platform's exact fonts, cropping, or caching behavior. Always confirm with the platform's own debugger before a big launch.

open-graph-preview.formula:
Tags this tool reads (first match wins per group):
Title: twitter:title -> og:title -> manual field
Description: twitter:description -> og:description -> manual field
Image: twitter:image -> og:image -> manual field
URL: og:url -> manual field
Card type: twitter:card = summary_large_image -> large, otherwise summary
(Manual fields override parsed tags when filled.)
howTo: Copy the <meta> tags from your page's <head> (View Source) and paste them into the box.
Or fill the manual fields directly to experiment — manual values override parsed tags.
Choose the X card type: Auto (from twitter:card), Summary, or Large image.
Review both previews: the X card and the Facebook/Open Graph card.
Fix any warnings (missing title, description, or image), update your page, then re-paste.
keyFacts: Social platforms build link cards from meta tags in your page <head> — they don't guess from visible content.
Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url) are the shared standard read by Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, and Telegram.
Twitter Card tags (twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:image) fine-tune how the card looks on X.
twitter:card values: summary (small thumbnail) or summary_large_image (wide banner).
og:image should be an absolute https:// URL, ideally 1200x630 px and under 5 MB.
Platforms cache cards for days — after fixing tags, use each platform's debugger to force a re-scrape.

open-graph-preview.quickAnswer: Paste your page's <meta> tags and this tool renders mock X and Facebook link cards from your og: and twitter: tags. It resolves the title (twitter:title, then og:title), description, image, and URL the same way platforms do, flags missing tags, and lets you override any value manually to experiment. For example, tags with twitter:card set to summary_large_image render the wide-banner X card.
open-graph-preview.tagline: Preview your X and Facebook link cards.
open-graph-preview.workedExample:
Sample pasted tags:
<meta property="og:title" content="Example — Free Browser Tools">
<meta property="og:description" content="Free tools that run in your browser.">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/og.png">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://example.com/">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
Resolved by the tool:
1. Title: Example — Free Browser Tools (from og:title; no twitter:title present).
2. Description: Free tools that run in your browser.
3. Image: https://example.com/og.png (https, so no warning).
4. URL/domain: example.com.
5. Card type: large (twitter:card = summary_large_image).
Result: the X preview shows the wide-banner layout; the Facebook preview shows the standard OG card. No warnings — all four core tags are present.
